papers.title: α-ketoglutarate ameliorates spinal motor neuron ferroptosis after sacral plexus transection via enhancing PINK1 O‑GlcNAcylation and mitophagy.
papers.summary: In a rat sacral plexus transection model, spinal motor neurons undergo ferroptosis (GPX4/SLC7A11 loss, iron overload, lipid peroxidation). α-ketoglutarate supplementation enhanced O-GlcNAcylation of PINK1 at Thr177, stabilizing it and activating PINK1-PRKN mitophagy, which improved neuronal survival; IDH1 downregulation was the upstream driver of endogenous AKG depletion.

papers.title: HMMR(+) stromal cells drive human uterine development.
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics of human fetal uterus (GW12-24) identified proliferative HMMR+ stromal cells that differentiate into stromal and muscle-like lineages, engraft in mice, and promote epithelial differentiation via pleiotrophin signaling. These cells are reduced in thin endometrium, defining a uterine stromal progenitor-like population relevant to endometrial pathology.

papers.title: A chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly for the barn owl, Tyto alba.
papers.summary: A chromosome-level, haplotype-resolved genome assembly for the western barn owl (Tyto alba) using trio-binning, PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore, and a linkage map yielded 46 chromosomes matching the karyotype, recovered six microchromosomes, and revealed a ~38 Mb complex inversion region on chromosome 7 — a reference for strigiformes and avian structural variation.

papers.title: Evolutionary diversification of invertase paralogs couples carbon metabolism and sexual reproduction in fission yeasts.
papers.summary: Across the fission yeast clade, an ancestral invertase duplication was followed by lineage-specific loss of one paralog, except Schizosaccharomyces pombe, which retains both. Inv1 is a secreted, glucose-repressed enzyme needed for sucrose assimilation; intracellular Inv2 induces sexual differentiation, linking carbon metabolism to the haploid-diploid cycle.

papers.title: Staphylococcus aureus biofilm infection impairs efferocytosis in wound-macrophages via induction of a MARCO(hi)MERTK(lo) subset.
papers.summary: Staphylococcus aureus biofilm-derived soluble cues — not bacterial contact — induce a MARCO(hi)MERTK(lo) wound macrophage subset that senses apoptotic cells but fails to engulf them, via nuclear C/EBPβ repressing MERTK. These cells populate 60-80% of infected chronic wounds; MARCO neutralization restored corpse clearance, nominating a druggable checkpoint.

papers.title: Atomistic TCR-pMHC interactions bias CD8 memory fate within a single antigen-specific repertoire.
papers.summary: Integrating single-cell transcriptomics, paired TCR sequencing, and force-dependent biophysics across 242 influenza NP366-374-specific murine CD8 TCR clonotypes, clonotype identity predicted central versus effector memory fates. Distinct Vα- versus Vβ-centric pMHC engagement altered force transmission, correlating with CD3ζ phosphorylation, expansion, and cross-reactivity, supporting TCR mechanochemistry in memory fate.

papers.title: Structure-based design of soluble prefusion-stabilized herpes simplex virus type 2 glycoprotein B antigens.
papers.summary: Using structure-based design, HSV-2 glycoprotein B was stabilized in its prefusion conformation, with a 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure revealing a closed prefusion state. Subunit and mRNA vaccines elicited robust responses; prefusion gB did not raise neutralizing titers versus postfusion but induced stronger FcγR-mediated effector functions, informing HSV-2 vaccine design.

papers.title: Berberine, a natural molecular glue degrader, overcomes CML resistance via TRIM28-mediated HIF1α ubiquitination and subsequent ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Berberine acts as a natural molecular glue degrader of HIF1α in BCR-ABL1-independent chronic myeloid leukemia: binding at HIF1α E816 recruits the E3 ligase TRIM28, driving K48-linked ubiquitination. HIF1α loss suppresses PDE4D, raises cAMP, depletes glutathione via the xCT axis, and with metal dyshomeostasis elevates ROS, triggering ferroptosis.

papers.title: Butyrophilin 3A1 engages the CDR2δ loop of the Vγ9Vδ2(+) T cell receptor.
papers.summary: Butyrophilin 3A1 directly binds the Vγ9Vδ2 TCR in a cell-free assay, confirming BTN3A1 as a direct ligand. Immobilized BTN2A1 plus BTN3A1 ectodomains suffice to activate Vδ2+ T cells, and intracellular phosphoantigen accumulation modulates TCR-BTN3A1 binding, defining the interactions required for phosphoantigen recognition by γδ T cells.

papers.title: Spatially ordered zygotic genome activation fulfills embryo quality control.
papers.summary: Spatially inverting the cell-size pattern of vertebrate blastulae flipped the spatial pattern of zygotic genome activation (ZGA); mispatterned ZGA triggered embryo apoptosis via a nonautonomous quality-control response dependent on an anti-apoptotic signal. Properly ordered ZGA is thus required for development, revealing surveillance tuned to genome-activation patterning.

papers.title: Clostridioides difficile couples responses to host nutritional immunity and a commensal-derived antibiotic to enable growth in the gut.
papers.summary: Clostridioides difficile carries a BCE membrane module incorporating the undecaprenyl pyrophosphatase BacA2 that senses the commensal-derived antibiotic bacitracin; Fur represses these genes, and low iron sensitizes cells to bacitracin. C. difficile integrates host nutritional immunity and bacitracin cues to maintain cell-envelope integrity and support gut colonization.

papers.title: Evaluating the pathogenic significance of unique chromosomal variants in craniosynostosis using patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells and mouse modelling.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.summary: For two families with craniosynostosis carrying structural variants potentially dysregulating FGF5 or FGF9, patient iPSC-derived neural crest and osteoprogenitor lines plus TAD modeling showed FGF upregulation (2.7-18x) and chromatin opening; a CRISPR-Cas9 mouse supported causality for dup(4)(q21.21), providing a functional framework for evaluating structural-variant pathogenicity.

papers.title: FM-GPT: Bayesian fine mapping for phenome-wide transcriptome-wide association studies.
papers.summary: FM-GPT is a Bayesian fine-mapping method for phenome-wide transcriptome-wide association studies that handles multiple correlated phenotypes with mixed outcome types. In simulations it outperformed other fine-mapping methods; UK Biobank applications identified pleiotropic genes for regional cortical thickness and multi-system clinical phenotypes, narrowing putative causal gene sets.

papers.title: ER-to-Golgi transport machinery promotes the excessive cargo-triggered unfolded protein response in C. elegans.
papers.summary: In C. elegans, neuronal overexpression of gap junction protein UNC-9 cell-autonomously activates the IRE-1-XBP-1 unfolded protein response. ER-to-Golgi proteins ERFI-2/ERGI-3 interact with UNC-9 and the chaperone HSP-4/BiP and are required cargo-selectively, coupling secretory cargo handling to adaptive UPR activation.

papers.title: Fission yeast RPA-TERT-Tpz1TPP1 complex promotes telomere extension and suppresses telomere recombination.
papers.summary: Genetic screens, AlphaFold3 modeling, and mutagenesis in fission yeast define a RPA-TRT1(TERT)-Tpz1(TPP1) ternary complex with four key interfaces that promote telomere extension and suppress recombination. RPA acts as an essential telomerase component coordinating TERT and TPP1-like factors, with these interfaces likely conserved in budding yeast and humans.

papers.title: Development of a low-coverage whole genome sequencing screen for apomixis using a diverse set of Malus germplasm.
papers.summary: A low-coverage (3x-6x) whole-genome sequencing screen for clonal seed production (apomixis) across a diverse USDA Malus germplasm collection sequenced 55 genotypes and 1,216 embryos, identifying 17 previously undescribed apomictic genotypes. Used alongside flow cytometry, it offers a rapid, low-cost screening approach with plant-breeding applications.

papers.title: Histone H3K9 methyltransferases regulate cortical growth by coordinating heterochromatin formation and neural progenitor dynamics.
papers.summary: A cortex-specific triple knockout of Setdb1, Suv39h1, and Suv39h2 in mice depleted H3K9me3 genome-wide, disrupting neural progenitor cell-cycle progression and causing microcephaly. These methyltransferases silence clustered protocadherins, meiosis genes, and cell-cycle restraints; transposable elements gained cryptic enhancer activity, establishing H3K9me3 heterochromatin as a regulator of cortical growth.

papers.title: Protein Age Bias in Target Degradation by PROTACs.
papers.summary: Using CG-SLENP chemical labeling of newly synthesized versus pre-existing proteins, this study shows PROTACs (dBET6, MZ-1, VZ185) preferentially degrade pre-existing BRD4/BRD9, while newly synthesized pools are degraded slowly and incompletely. Protein age is an unrecognized determinant of degrader efficacy, explaining incomplete clearance and rebound kinetics in targeted protein degradation.

papers.title: In vitro evaluation of hydroxyapatite, β-tricalcium phosphate, graphene oxide and zinc oxide for osteochondral regeneration under inflammatory conditions.
papers.summary: Hydroxyapatite, β-TCP, graphene oxide, and zinc oxide were tested on osteoblast- and chondrocyte-like cells under IL-1β inflammatory conditions. All maintained basal matrix synthesis while suppressing ECM-degrading enzymes; graphene oxide was chondroprotective, whereas zinc oxide impaired mineralization via RUNX2 cytoplasmic trapping, supporting layer-specific biomaterial integration for osteochondral repair.

papers.title: Modeling meningioma in vitro in the omics era.
papers.summary: This review integrates omics-based meningioma subgrouping with functional in vitro studies, covering established cell lines, 3D models, and organoids, and organizing mechanistic findings into six signaling pathways (Hippo, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK, WNT/β-catenin, FOXM1, Notch), while discussing modeling challenges such as immortalization artifacts and culture drift from parental tumors.

papers.title: Defined O-acetylated Neu5Ac substrates reveal position-specific preferences of gut bacterial sialidases.
papers.summary: Six GH33 sialidases from Bacteroides spp. and Akkermansia muciniphila were profiled on defined 4-, 7-, and 8/9-O-acetylated Neu5Ac substrates. All cleaved 8/9-O-acetylated Neu5Ac but none cleaved the 4-O-acetylated form; viral esterase treatment restored cleavage, revealing position-specific, enzyme-dependent processing of O-acetylated sialic acid in the gut.

papers.title: Neuroligin 3 highlights the sexually dimorphic neural substrates of Drosophila social spacing.
papers.summary: Neuroligin 3 acts in Drosophila mushroom bodies, optic lobes, and protocerebral bridge to shape social spacing, with clear sex specificity: hyperactivation or silencing increased female social space, whereas only hyperactivation affected males. Cholinergic and dopaminergic manipulations and fruitless neurons further delineate sexually dimorphic neural substrates of social behavior.

papers.title: Evidence of genome-wide relaxed selection on mildly deleterious mutations in an ancient subterranean catfish.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Genome sequencing of four Peruvian subterranean catfishes and surface relatives shows contrasting decay of light-related genes (1%-48% pseudogenes) and molecular dates spanning early Pliocene to late Pleistocene, supporting repeated cave colonization. The oldest species shows genome-wide relaxed purifying selection, consistent with long-term small effective population size.

papers.title: Reference genome of the Californian trapdoor spider Aptostichus stephencolberti Bond 2008 (Araneae: Mygalomorphae: Euctenizidae).
papers.summary: A reference genome for the Californian trapdoor spider Aptostichus stephencolberti spans 3.63 Gbp in 551 scaffolds with 95.6% BUSCO completeness, ~52 chromosomes, and 14,067 annotated genes. The first Euctenizidae genome, it reveals ancestral loss of (TTAGG)n telomere repeats and supports conservation genomics of fragmented coastal dune habitats.

papers.title: Beyond traditional criteria: CRP and fibrinogen as biomarkers of metabolic syndrome in ART-treated people living with HIV and their association with HIF-1α rs11549465.
papers.summary: In a Serbian multicenter case-control study of 116 people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy, CRP and fibrinogen were elevated in metabolic syndrome with proposed cutoffs (1.85 mg/L and 2.49 g/L), and the HIF-1α rs11549465 CT+TT genotype associated with higher IL-6, supporting inflammation-marker complement to standard criteria.

papers.title: Ketogenic diet-induced changes in hepatic drug metabolism with potential implications for ozanimod pharmacokinetics in mice.
papers.summary: In mice, a 4-week ketogenic diet induced ketosis, raised plasma cholesterol, altered gut microbiota, and changed hepatic cytochrome P450 expression and activity, including increased CYP1A relevant to ozanimod metabolism. Ozanimod exposure showed a non-significant ~17% AUC increase, highlighting potential diet-drug interactions in multiple sclerosis therapy.

papers.title: Introducing a proline in the α1 M2-M3 linker relieves a molecular brake on channel activation in α1β2γ2 GABAA receptors.
papers.summary: Introducing a proline at the α1 M2-M3 linker site 2 (A280P) of α1β2γ2 GABAA receptors enhanced GABA sensitivity and spontaneous channel activity in Xenopus oocytes, while β2 proline replacements had variable effects, indicating that conserved M2-M3 linker prolines act as a molecular brake on channel activation.

papers.title: Anatomy-aware, label-informed approach improves image registration for challenging datasets.
papers.summary: A label-informed image registration approach in the ANTsX ecosystem uses anatomical segmentations to guide regional correspondence, enabling registration of knockout mouse embryos with overt phenotypes (e.g., gli2-/- scoliosis) that fail traditional intensity-based methods, improving interpretability, power, and sensitivity of registration-based morphometrics in developmental and comparative datasets.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven identification and mechanistic exploration of synergistic anti-aging compounds from Dengzhan Shengmai formulation.
papers.summary: DeepSMCA, a deep learning framework combining molecular descriptors, ADMET parameters, PPI network embeddings, and Bliss independence, identified synergistic anti-aging compound combinations from the Dengzhan Shengmai formulation. Three combinations validated in senescent PC12 cells improved viability, reduced oxidative stress and senescence markers, and reversed aging-related transcriptional changes across longevity, FOXO, p53, and autophagy pathways.

papers.title: BICC1 attenuates oxidative stress-induced osteogenic injury via regulation of the PDK/PDH axis in MC3T3-E1 cells.
papers.summary: In an H2O2-induced oxidative injury model of MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, BICC1 overexpression alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis, restored osteogenic differentiation, and inhibited the PDK1/PDH axis; PDK1 inhibition with dichloroacetate recapitulated the protection, nominating BICC1 as a potential therapeutic target for oxidative stress-driven bone disease.

papers.title: DNA methylation-mediated silencing of MALAT1 promotes dexamethasone-induced growth plate chondrocyte ferroptosis via miR-124-3p/LPCAT3.
papers.summary: Dexamethasone hypermethylates the MALAT1 promoter, reducing MALAT1 and promoting growth plate chondrocyte ferroptosis via miR-124-3p targeting of LPCAT3. MALAT1 overexpression or 5-aza demethylation restored SLC7A11/GPX4, lowered iron and lipid peroxidation markers, and ameliorated growth plate deficits in rats, identifying a preclinical epigenetic therapeutic axis.

papers.title: Influenza A virus neuraminidase-GRP78 binding site prediction.
papers.summary: Docking and molecular dynamics predict that influenza A neuraminidase binds the host chaperone GRP78 via a conserved cysteine-cyclized region VIII (C278:C291), with H3N2 neuraminidase remaining stably associated with GRP78's substrate-binding domain during simulation, identifying a potential therapeutic target for neutralizing seasonal H3N2 neuraminidase.

papers.title: Unravelling genetic diversity, population connectivity, and evolutionary relationships of Indian mealybugs through mtCO1-based phylogenetic and haplotype analyses.
papers.summary: Integrative mtCO1 barcoding of 134 Indian mealybug specimens resolved 14 species across eight genera with species-specific clades. Phenacoccus solenopsis and Planococcus minor showed multiple haplotypes and geographic structuring, with demographic evidence of recent expansion in some regions, supporting species identification, invasion monitoring, and biosecurity surveillance.

papers.title: Signal recognition particle 14 binds to importin α in Plasmodium falciparum.
papers.summary: This study reports the first direct binding between a eukaryotic signal recognition particle 14 (SRP14) and importin α, demonstrated for Plasmodium falciparum with recombinant proteins in glutathione-agarose and 96-well plate binding assays, supporting nuclear import roles in SRP biogenesis and providing a cost-effective cargo-binding assay.

papers.title: Dimethyl phthalate induces cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and fibronectin accumulation in A549 lung epithelial cells.
papers.summary: Dimethyl phthalate exposure of A549 lung epithelial cells caused concentration- and time-dependent cytotoxicity, elevated intracellular and mitochondrial ROS, necrotic death, increased TNF-α/IL-6/IL-8 expression and secretion, and fibronectin accumulation, mirroring pathways implicated in chronic respiratory diseases such as COPD and underscoring pulmonary phthalate toxicity concerns.

papers.title: Macrophage heterogeneity in organ fibrosis in the era of single-cell omics.
papers.summary: Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, this review builds a multidimensional framework of macrophage heterogeneity in organ fibrosis across lung, liver, kidney, and heart. SPP1+ stroma-associated macrophages emerge as a conserved pro-fibrotic end-state, while metabolic reprogramming (e.g., the glycolysis-PKM2 axis) shapes macrophage fate and therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title: Protease inhibition: breaking the barriers of chemoresistance in cancer.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how matrix metalloproteinases, cathepsins, ubiquitin-specific proteases, proteasome components, and mitochondrial proteases drive chemoresistance through drug transport, ECM remodeling, EMT, and apoptosis. Broad-spectrum protease inhibition has had limited clinical success; context-specific targeting, biomarker-guided selection, combinations, and delivery platforms may overcome these barriers.

papers.title: Integrated Proteomics and Metabolomics Analysis Reveals Regulatory Mechanisms Underlying Flower Bud Development in Camellia drupifera.
papers.summary: Integrated proteomics and metabolomics across three floral bud stages of Camellia drupifera showed declining IAA, ABA, and ACC with stage-dependent GA3 changes, upregulated energy-metabolism proteins supporting ATP production, and downregulated tryptophan-metabolism enzymes explaining reduced IAA, clarifying metabolic regulation of floral bud development in this woody oil crop.

papers.title: Thymoquinone as a Multi-Target Modulator of Inflammatory and Immunometabolic Signaling: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.summary: This review examines thymoquinone, the principal Nigella sativa bioactive, across three interconnected immunometabolic axes: NF-κB-mediated inflammation, AMPK/mTOR metabolic regulation, and ROS/NRF2 redox balance. Preclinical evidence supports multi-target modulation and pathway crosstalk, though the proposed framework remains hypothesis-generating pending integrated experimental and clinical validation.

papers.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Attenuates Fibrotic and Inflammatory Dermal Remodelling in a Bleomycin-Induced Skin Model.
papers.summary: In a bleomycin-induced rat skin fibrosis model, alpha-lipoic acid (50 mg/kg/day) attenuated epidermal thickening, inflammatory infiltration, collagen deposition, and mast cell density, and reduced collagen I/III, IL-6, iNOS, caspase-1, and Ki-67 immunoreactivity, suggesting protection against bleomycin-induced dermal remodeling pending mechanistic confirmation.

papers.title: Necrosis by Sodium Overload: Mechanisms, Pathophysiological Roles, and Therapeutic Prospects of a Novel Form of Regulated Cell Death.
papers.summary: Necrosis by sodium overload (NecSo), coined in 2025, is a regulated necrosis form triggered by sustained Na+ influx primarily via TRPM4, causing mitochondrial energy collapse and membrane rupture without caspase activation. It mediates ischemia-reperfusion myocardial injury, heart failure, and stroke, with tissue-specific dual roles in cancer.

papers.title: Beyond a Surface Marker: The Multifaceted Role of CD38 in Metabolic Disruption and Tumor Progression.
papers.summary: CD38, the primary NAD+ ectoenzyme, influences immunosuppression, aging-related NAD+ depletion, and exosomal signaling. This review covers its enzymatic functions, pathophysiological roles in hematological and solid tumors, resistance mechanisms to anti-CD38 therapies, and its potential as an exosomal liquid-biopsy biomarker and metabolic resetter for healthy aging.

papers.title: From Glycation to Toxicity: α-Synuclein Oligomers, Oxidative Stress, and Multi-Targeted Protection by Trans-Ferulic Acid.
papers.summary: α-Synuclein glycation by methylglyoxal drives aggregation, impaired clearance, and AGE-RAGE-mediated oxidative and inflammatory damage in Parkinson's disease. Trans-ferulic acid inhibited glycation in ribose- and methylglyoxal-induced α-synuclein systems, scavenged hydrogen peroxide and nitric oxide, and inhibited α-glucosidase, acting as a multi-target agent against glycation-driven toxicity.
